evidence.note: The page states 38 years, 1749–1712, and says Hammu-rabi dates follow the average chronology.
The lecture series is explicitly about Hammu-rabi’s successors and names Samsu-iluna among them.

UNESCO identifies these coordinates for the Babylon World Heritage property. Converted N32 32 31.09 E44 25 15 to decimal degrees; the passage does not establish a historical association between Babylon and Samsu-iluna.
The ministry page identifies Rîm-Sîn and gives his reign; in this early second-millennium Larsa context this is Rim-Sin I. The page does not discuss Rim-Sin II.
The ministry directly links Rîm-Sîn’s reign with Larsa’s apogee.
The page says Babylon under Hammurabi took Larsa in 1763; this is a political connection, not a claim of personal meeting.
The Met’s title supplies a broad regional period span; using it for the city is explicitly editorial, and does not claim continuous occupation.
The source explicitly names the ruins of ancient Larsa as Tell es Senkereh.
The French Ministry page identifies Tell es Senkereh as ancient Larsa and places it in the Lower Mesopotamian plain between the Tigris and Euphrates. No numeric coordinates are given.
The ministry directly associates Rim-Sin’s reign with Larsa’s apogee.
